newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa's Mbeki delays flight to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Mbeki delays flight to Zaire.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki postponed his departure for Zaire on Tuesday, but an aide said he remained confident that an accord between the country's warring leaders was possible.

"The deputy president has delayed his departure for Zaire to complete consultations on the peace process, but he is quite confident it will be possible to reach a broad agreement on a framework for the transition process," the aide told Reuters.

Ricky Naidoo, a spokesman for Mbeki, said the deputy president was in touch with representatives of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel rival Laurent Kabila, who are scheduled to meet face-to-face for the second time on Wednesday.

President Nelson Mandela, who brought them together for the first time on May 4, is scheduled to chair the meeting aboard the South African navy ice-breaker Outeniqua in or near the Congolese port of Pointe Noire.
Mandela told reporters in Cape Town he was confident of success "...as long as everybody understands that this is not an event, it is a process."
Naidoo said Mbeki was consulting South African foreign ministry officials and representatives of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.
"He's quite confident at the moment that it is possible to achieve agreement on a broad framework for the transition which can be ratified on the boat," he said.
Naidoo said Mbeki expected to know late on Tuesday afternoon whether the meeting would go ahead as planned on Wednesday, but he added:
"The meeting will definitely go ahead. Right now its about 80 percent certain it will go ahead on Wednesday."
Naidoo said Mbeki was likely to leave late on Tuesday for Kabila's rebel headquarters in Lubumbashi and later for Kinshasa to see Mobutu.
